acceptance: Repro script or log evidence showing a run with --force datagen (or fresh datagen in-phase) produces a manifest the load phase resolves to zero valid files
Fix verified by a live or integration run where same-invocation datagen loads all tables without a warm rerun
No shared datagen cache clobbered by the fix verification
context: Observed 2026-09-29/30 on cloud BigQuery runs: an isolated gzip datagen dir held a fresh v2 manifest plus valid .gz shards (manifest compression gzip, files present with size), yet the load phase logged 'Skipping <table> - no valid data files' for every multi-file table while single-file tables (nation, region) loaded. A warm rerun against the same cache loaded all tables (CUSTOMER 15000 rows from 10 files). Same pattern on read_primitives SF0.01 2026-09-30: fresh-cache run failed validation with empty tables, warm rerun loaded in 57s and passed validation. Static probes of ManifestFileSource, get_table_files, DataSourceResolver, and BenchmarkTablesSource all resolved correctly outside the run, so the defect is in run-time sequencing or state, not path resolution. BigQuery lane only so far; unknown whether other adapters share it. Workaround documented: two-phase runs (generate, then warm rerun) with isolated BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR for gzip.
description: A benchmark run that generates datagen files in-phase (fresh cache, --force datagen, or first run into an empty dir) can reach the load phase with a manifest the loader does not resolve: BigQuery logs 'Skipping <table> - no valid data files' for multi-file tables and validation fails on empty tables, even though the manifest and shard files are valid on disk. A warm rerun against the same cache loads correctly. Investigate the generate-to-load handoff (manifest re-read timing, benchmark.tables population vs data_dir resolution, DataSourceResolver provider ordering at load time), reproduce with a minimal local case if possible, fix so same-invocation datagen loads, and add a regression test.
